Compartment 4.16.1 ships Apple Developer ID code signing, macOS Hardened Runtime, Apple Notarization (`xcrun notarytool`), and stapled Gatekeeper tickets (`xcrun stapler`) across both Apple silicon and Intel macOS `.app`, `.dmg`, and `.pkg` installers, 100% offline at runtime, with zero network calls of any kind and a portable, encrypted `.vault` file you own and can back up or copy anywhere, local disk, USB, NAS, or any cloud drive, like any other file.

## What's New

### Apple Developer ID Signing, Hardened Runtime, and Notarization for macOS
- **No Gatekeeper warnings on first launch:** Both Apple silicon (`Compartment-4.16.1.dmg` and `Compartment-4.16.1.pkg`) and Intel (`Compartment-4.16.1-intel.dmg` and `Compartment-4.16.1-intel.pkg`) downloads are now signed with Apple Developer ID Application and Developer ID Installer certificates, notarized by Apple (`xcrun notarytool`), and stapled (`xcrun stapler`) so macOS Gatekeeper verifies them offline and online out of the box without requiring `System Settings > Privacy & Security > Open Anyway`.
- **Hardened Runtime with macOS Library Validation preserved:** Every nested Mach-O dynamic library (`.dylib` and `.so`), the embedded standalone Python 3.12 runtime binary, and the native `Compartment.app` launcher are signed deepest-path-first with secure timestamps under macOS Hardened Runtime (`--options runtime`), granting only `com.apple.security.cs.allow-unsigned-executable-memory` for `PyObjC` and `libffi` closures while keeping macOS Library Validation enabled across the entire bundle.
- **Clean contributor fallback and automated release verification:** `tools/build_macos_app.py` adds `--sign-auto`, `--sign-app`, `--sign-pkg`, and `--notarize` (falling back automatically to ad-hoc signing when Developer ID credentials are absent so local contributor builds and tests need no Apple account), and `.github/workflows/release.yml` validates stapled tickets on both `macos-latest` and `macos-15-intel` before drafting every release.
